messages:
kevin: Hi all, I'm two days in and trying to finish device setup. Received a used MBP (Intel) from IT but after enrolling it the FileVault toggle is greyed out and system prefs says 'No secure token users'. Also the login screen shows two accounts: kevin (local) and previous-owner. Any tips?

it-support: welcome kevin! that's a common hand-me-down issue. If there's another local account that owns the SecureToken, FileVault enable will be blocked for your user. Do you see the previous owner account on the Users & Groups pane?

kevin: yes there's an account 'olivia-legacy' listed but it's disabled. I don't have that password.

rachel: hey, if 'olivia-legacy' still has a SecureToken we need to either re-enable it to transfer token or create a new temp admin via MDM and grant your user a token. Do you want us to push the temp admin or try recovering the legacy user?

kevin: prefer not to recover olivia. push temp admin please.

it-support: ok pushing rdw-rotate-admin (expires 3hr). We'll also schedule a short screenshare to walk through `sysadminctl -secureTokenOn`.

mdm-bot: MDM command CreateLocalAdmin rdw-rotate-admin issued for serial=C02DXYAAAA at 09:05 PT

it-support: got the cmd through. Please open Terminal and run `sudo sysadminctl -addUser rdw-rotate-admin -fullName "Rotating Admin" -password Temp$ecure1 -admin` and use your password to authorize when prompted.

kevin: done, it asked for my password and added the account.

it-support: great. Now from the new admin run: `sudo sysadminctl -secureTokenOn kevin -password <your_pw> -adminUser rdw-rotate-admin -adminPassword Temp$ecure1`

kevin: ran it. returned exit 0. Checked `sysadminctl -secureTokenStatus kevin` -> "Secure token is ENABLED for user kevin"

it-support: perfect. Next `sudo fdesetup enable -user kevin` which will print a recovery key. Keep it private while MDM escrows it.

kevin: ran it, got the long key. mdm-bot: "Recovery escrow received serial=C02DXYAAAA user=kevin status=SUCCESS"

mdm-bot: Compliance update: serial=C02DXYAAAA compliance=COMPLIANT FDE=MANAGED

kevin: console now green. thanks! quick follow-up: what about olivia-legacy account? can it be deleted?

it-support: yes, we will wipe that account. Since it was a leftover, we'll remove it and purge its home folder. We'll back up anything that looks company-related first (none expected). Proceeding to delete olivia-legacy.

mdm-bot: Local user removal scheduled: olivia-legacy for serial=C02DXYAAAA by it-support at 09:42 PT

kevin: saw a warning about re-authorizing Mail and some keychain items after the deletion. Is that normal?

devops: yep, when the home dir is purged the system may prompt you to re-enter passwords for Wi-Fi, Git credentials, or saved keys. If anything critical is missing ping us and we can restore specific items from the handover snapshot.

kevin: all good so far, only had to re-enter Okta SSO password once. One more question: my Touch ID fingerprint disappeared after we created the temp admin. Is that expected?

it-support: Touch ID profiles are stored per-user and can be reset during admin operations; you can re-add fingerprints in Settings > Touch ID & Password. Nothing to worry about.

kevin: re-added, worked. Thanks for the help! tagging this thread for future hand-me-down devices.

it-support: note: ticket IT-5099 created with steps: temp admin creation -> secureTokenOn -> enable fdesetup -> remove legacy account. We'll add a short KB to the new-hires docs. Closing in 48h if no issues. :white_check_mark:
